title: Identification of IDH3G, encoding the gamma subunit of mitochondrial isocitrate dehydrogenase, as a novel candidate gene for X-linked retinitis pigmentosa.

reviewer.method: Read the entire 14-page published paper, including references and disclosures, all five main figures and Table 1; read the entire five-page supplement and all Supplementary Figures 1-5. Inspected all 19 full-page renders and additional S3 crops. Compared both assigned selected packets, both variant descriptors and all 20 phenotype items. No alternate packets are assigned. This is source-correspondence review, not clinical reclassification or new experimental analysis.

audit.exposure_note: Successor inherits prior parent-session exposure to individual-case outcome-linked work and aggregate benchmark results. Per-case exposure is retained conservatively; this review is post-inference, non-blinded and not preregistered. No ranking outputs were newly opened during this narrowly scoped source reading.

components.note: S1: three alignment blocks, eight species, four marked residues and mismatches. S2: bilateral B65/C60/D69 fundus images. S3: all four 5x3 grids (IDH3G/Myc, IDH3G/ATP-beta, COX5B/Myc, IDH3G/Mitotracker), WT plus four variants; Gln377* tag absence retained. causal_confidence.statement: The packet explicitly assigns ACMG PATHOGENIC and SOLVED/CAUSATIVE. The source formally classifies this variant as LIKELY PATHOGENIC (Table 1 and page 10), and states that further research is needed to confirm the IDH3G-XLRP association. The formal pathogenicity level therefore disagrees; this does not falsify the proposed diagnosis.

evidence.locator: Table 1 page 8, LP classification; Discussion/conclusion page 10; functional limits pages 6 and 9.

limitations: Both variants have lower protein expression in COS-1 overexpression experiments, but no statistically significant respiration decrease was demonstrated; patient-derived mechanistic validation is not supplied.
The later OMIM disease name/identifier in the packet is not independently established by this article; current external classification was outside this source-only audit.

phenotype_completeness.statement: All assigned phenotype items, negatives and onset annotations were checked. The packet is a selected feature abstraction: severe rod/cone dysfunction on full-field ERG, retained central macular function and absence of relevant systemic conditions are additionally discussed. The article gives no exhaustive patient-level clinical table. Disease label RP99/OMIM:301148 is a later annotation not verified in this article.

access_issues.detail: Official full main and sole supplementary PDF acquired by parent; hashes reverified and all published components read by successor. No contact or browser use performed.

evidence.locator: Exact URLs, byte counts and SHA256 values for published.pdf and supplement.pdf.
Both PDF page counts verified.

limitations: Post-inference, per-case-exposed, non-blinded source audit; this does not clinically validate the benchmark or independently replicate laboratory results.

Paper proposes a candidate association with five unrelated probands. Reduced protein abundance is not a measured reduction in enzymatic activity; the Seahorse result was not statistically significant.
No underlying raw genomic, perimetry, blot densitometry or Seahorse data were obtained; only the published components are complete.
Supplementary alignment and protein models are inspected evidence, not newly computed predictions. Figure 5 bars were not digitized or used as exact quantitative measurements.

Both packets have a formal PATHOGENIC versus source LP disagreement. A additionally has the peripheral-field wording conflict; D's negative ring-scotoma assertion is unresolved. Frozen packets are unchanged.
